purpose: Implements conversation-mode context-window management for @mention threads: per-thread turn tracking with a maxTurns auto-close, a sliding message window condensed into incremental LLM summary snapshots via a shared estimateTokens utility, budget enforcement and warnings in the prompt builder, per-thread locking with TTL/capacity-bounded in-memory state, and configurable limits via env vars and a new yml conversation section.
riskRationale: The mechanics are well-built and well-tested (43 passing unit tests plus new engine-level orchestration tests, clean typecheck/lint), and nearly every prior finding landed: incremental summarization, fresh-flag coverage gating, alreadyClosed dedup, per-comment scratch dirs, telemetry for summary runs, TTL/capacity-bounded state, per-thread locks, and full env/yml/summarizationModel wiring. Three design-level bugs remain that defeat the feature's core purpose for the most common flows: review-comment conversation state is keyed on the triggering comment id so turns never accumulate (auto-close and incremental summarization are inert); issue-level mentions share one state and their capped thread makes the summary go stale with silent context drops; and the token-budget enforcement loop cannot reduce a prompt once a summary snapshot exists. No security issues found.
breakingChanges: ConversationConfig gained three required fields (maxTurns, slidingWindowSize, contextTokenBudget), so external code constructing a literal ConversationConfig must add them
Threads longer than slidingWindowSize are now trimmed from the conversation prompt (with an omission note / summary preamble), changing the prompt the model sees for long threads
The review-comment threadId now includes a comment suffix, so conversation state (turns, summaries) no longer persists across turns of a single discussion

New CONVERSATION_MAX_TURNS / CONVERSATION_SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE / CONVERSATION_CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET / CONVERSATION_SUMMARIZATION_MODEL env vars and a new conversation section in .opencode-reviewer.yml (action only)

text: A disciplined, well-tested iteration that resolves most prior findings: summarization is incremental and bounded (O(window) not O(thread)), coverage advances only on genuinely fresh snapshots, already-closed threads no-op, per-thread locks serialize turns, state is TTL/capacity-bounded, summary runs record telemetry, summarizationModel is fully wired, and new engine-level tests exercise runConversation orchestration — all 43 tests pass with clean typecheck/lint. The remaining blockers are concentrated in the handler/prompt design: the review-comment threadId resets state every turn, issue threads both share one state and go stale beyond the window with silent context drops, and the token-budget halving loop cannot shrink a prompt once a summary snapshot exists.

reasoning: Three important design-level bugs remain: review-comment state is keyed per-trigger-comment-id so it resets every turn (defeating turn counting, auto-close, and incremental summarization for the primary use case), issue threads are capped at the window so summaries go stale and context silently drops, and the budget-enforcement loop is a no-op whenever a summary exists so long threads can still overflow the model context window. These need design-level fixes (root-comment thread keys, cumulative issue-thread gathering, budget enforcement that actually bounds re-rendered content) and are not safe as one-click automated fixes.

message: Incremental summarization is done right: only messages added since the last snapshot are sent (olderMessages.slice(covered)) and the existing summarySnapshot is passed as 'Existing Summary' for the model to merge into, bounding the summary prompt to O(window) instead of O(thread length).

The {text, fresh} return contract plus unlink-before-run is a correct failure-handling pattern: a stale conversation-summary.txt can never be reused as a 'fresh' snapshot, coverage only advances on a genuinely fresh write, and a failed run keeps prior coverage so shouldSummarize re-triggers instead of silently dropping rolled-out messages.

withThreadLock serializes per-thread turns without blocking other threads, the finally-guard only deletes the lock entry when it is still the current waiter (correct for the chained-lock case), and TTL pruning plus capacity-based eviction bound the in-memory map — a genuinely solid concurrency/memory design.

The new engine-level tests are the right kind of coverage: they mock runOpenCode/fs and assert real orchestration behavior (auto-close short-circuits the model call, empty replies do not consume a turn or trigger a summary pass, failed summaries preserve coverage, state is isolated per threadId) rather than only testing pure functions.

Extracting estimateTokens into a shared utility removes the duplicated private copy in mcp/client.ts and keeps the MCP trims and conversation budgeting on the same ~4-char/token heuristic so they cannot drift.

Checking shouldAutoClose before launching a model call is a clean cost guard — closed threads answer with a pre-formatted message instead of burning tokens, and the alreadyClosed flag returns '' so the handler skips duplicate close-message spam.

The conversation env-var block reuses the established parseEnvInt/clampInt pattern, and its clamp ranges exactly match the zod schema and validateConfig bounds, while summarizationModel is wired end-to-end (env var + yml schema + action consumption) — so the app env path and the action yml path cannot silently diverge and the model override is no longer always undefined.

The thread-identity scheme breaks state continuity for both comment flows. For review-comment threads, threadId is keyed on the *triggering* comment id (`#${commentId}`), but GitHub assigns a new id to every reply in a thread, so each turn resolves to a brand-new ConversationState (turnCount 0, no summarySnapshot): maxTurns auto-close never accumulates, summaries are stored under a state that is never read again, and — because summarizedCount is always 0 — every overflow turn re-sends the ENTIRE older chunk to the summarizer, re-paying O(threadLen) cost per turn. For issue-level mentions, threadId is `${repo}/${prNumber}/issue` for every @mention on the PR, so unrelated discussions share one turnCount, one summary snapshot, and one alreadyClosed flag: after maxTurns total mentions the conversation auto-closes for everyone, each mention's summary can be injected into another discussion's prompt, and a single alreadyClosed flag can be set by one thread. The prior shared-file key at least accumulated turns; this over-corrects to per-message granularity for review threads while leaving issue threads collapsed.
suggestion: Key review threads on the ROOT comment id (the oldest in_reply_to ancestor returned by gatherReviewThread) so turns within one discussion accumulate while distinct threads stay isolated, and isolate issue mentions by their own comment id so unrelated issue conversations stop sharing turn counts and summaries.

message: gatherIssueCommentThread caps the accumulated issue thread at slidingWindowSize+1 (21) messages, and index-based summarizedCount goes stale on the shifting issue chain. threadLength stays pinned at ~21 so olderCount is always 1: shouldSummarize fires once for a single message, stores summarizedCount=1, and the doubling heuristic (olderCount >= covered*2) never fires again. As the window slides, each turn's new oldest message is neither in the fetched thread, nor covered by the stale summary, nor in the recent window — it is silently dropped from the model's context every turn. The sliding-window/summarization machinery is effectively dead for the most common @mention flow, and the handler's claim that long issue threads 'overflow the sliding window and can be summarized' is not borne out by the implementation.
suggestion: Decouple the accumulation size from the engine window so issue threads can actually overflow (e.g. accumulate 2x slidingWindowSize), and track summary coverage by a stable message identity/cursor (last summarized comment id) instead of a positional index so the summary keeps up with the sliding window.

message: The token-budget enforcement loop is ineffective whenever a summarySnapshot exists. 'uncoveredOlderMessages' is rendered verbatim as 'recently rolled out', and uncovered + recent together always equal thread messages [summarizedCount..end) regardless of windowSize — halving the window merely moves messages from the recent section into the uncovered section, so estimatedTokens stays constant. Verified empirically on a 100-message thread with a 50-message summary: the assembled prompt estimates ~4518 tokens for window sizes 20, 10, 5, 2 and 1 — identical and still over budget. On long threads with a summary the 'Context Usage ~N / budget' footer is cosmetic and the prompt can blow past the model's context window, exactly what this feature exists to prevent; the only budget test passes no state, so the summary path is never exercised.
suggestion: Only render uncovered older messages when the window is at its configured size; when budget pressure shrinks the window, omit the 'recently rolled out' section entirely (those messages will be folded into the summary on the next summarization pass), and add a test whose state carries a summarySnapshot plus uncovered messages to prove the loop actually shrinks the prompt.

message: manager.updateState(state, undefined, undefined, 3) passes a 4th argument to the 3-parameter signature (state, latestSummary, summarizedCount), which ignores it. This would be a TS2554 error under strict mode, but lib/tsconfig.json includes only src/** so tests are never typechecked; vitest silently drops the extra arg, so the intended summarizedCount=3 is never applied and the test only proves the trivially-true fact that updateState leaves alreadyClosed untouched.
suggestion: Drop the 4th argument — a plain updateState(state) suffices for the alreadyClosed-preservation assertion — or call updateState(state, 'summary', 3) and assert state.summarizedCount is 3.

message: State is held only in memory, so any app restart wipes turnCount and alreadyClosed. A thread that was already auto-closed silently resurrects (turnCount resets to 0) and, after another maxTurns cycle, posts a second auto-close message — a closed conversation never returns the stable '' no-op the engine assumes after restart. The in-memory design is documented, but the 'closed once, forever silent' behavior vs reset-on-restart is inconsistent and surprising.
suggestion: Persist per-thread alreadyClosed (and ideally turnCount/summary) in the learning store or a small SQLite table so closure is durable across restarts; at minimum, log a warning when a previously-closed thread resumes after a restart.

message: getOrCreateState calls pruneExpiredStates(), a full synchronous iteration of the states Map, on every webhook turn. With up to MAX_STATES entries and a long-lived subscriber handling many repos, this is O(n) bookkeeping per mention with no incremental index; harmless at current scale but easy to avoid.
suggestion: Run pruning lazily — only every N calls or only when the map is at/near capacity — or maintain a min-heap of lastActivityTimestamp for O(log n) eviction.

message: CONVERSATION_MENTION_HANDLE is stored verbatim, but the subscriber matches mentions by prefixing '@' (app/src/subscribers/conversation.ts builds `@${mentionHandle}` and handlers strip a leading '@'). A user naturally setting CONVERSATION_MENTION_HANDLE=@mybot makes the check test for '@@mybot', silently disabling conversation mode with no warning.
suggestion: Normalize the value by stripping a leading '@' before storing, e.g. (process.env.CONVERSATION_MENTION_HANDLE || DEFAULT_CONFIG.conversation.mentionHandle).replace(/^@/, ''), so both '@handle' and 'handle' inputs behave identically.

message: The five new conversation env vars are undocumented in .env.example (the canonical app env reference lists RATE_LIMIT_* etc. but none of the CONVERSATION_* vars), and README.md:209 lists only four of them, omitting CONVERSATION_MENTION_HANDLE — so the only way to discover it is reading source.
suggestion: Add a 'Conversation (Probot App only)' section to .env.example covering CONVERSATION_MENTION_HANDLE, CONVERSATION_MAX_TURNS, CONVERSATION_SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE, CONVERSATION_CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET, and CONVERSATION_SUMMARIZATION_MODEL, and append CONVERSATION_MENTION_HANDLE to the README env-var list.

message: The new buildConfig() conversation env-var parsing/clamping (parseEnvInt + clampInt + the conditional summarizationModel spread) has zero test coverage — grep for buildConfig across app/tests and action/tests returns nothing, and there is no app/tests/config.test.ts. The clamping is non-trivial enough (0 vs unlimited maxTurns, lower-bound raising, blank-model omission) to warrant tests.
suggestion: Add unit tests for buildConfig() (e.g. app/tests/config.test.ts) covering: default fallback when env is unset, clamp boundaries (CONVERSATION_MAX_TURNS=0 → unlimited, out-of-range clamped), blank CONVERSATION_SUMMARIZATION_MODEL being omitted, and a leading-@ mention handle being normalized.
